//: NOTHING SECRET GOES IN THIS FILE — it is committed.
SQL password  -> SQL_PASSWORD environment variable (only needed for SQL auth).
SMTP password -> SMTP_PASSWORD environment variable.
JWT key       -> dotnet user-secrets set "Jwt:Key" "<64+ chars>"
JP.Sso.Api configures the Sso connection only. It never opens jp_mdm or
jp_app, which is what lets it be deployed on its own.

ConnectionStrings.//: Server and database only. Encryption, timeouts and Application Name are applied by DbConnectionFactory from the Database section below.

//: Encrypt defaults to true in Microsoft.Data.SqlClient 4.0+.
TrustServerCertificate MUST stay false here — appsettings.Development.json
turns it on for localhost\TARUN, which presents a self-signed certificate.
Leaving it on against a real server would accept any certificate and
defeat the protection encryption is there to provide.

Jwt.//: Key is deliberately absent. Set it in user-secrets or an environment variable.

//: Fixed windows, counted PER PROCESS. Behind more than one instance each
node counts separately, so the effective limit is these numbers times
the instance count — a shared store is the fix, and is not Phase 1C.
Login carries two limits at once: per IP stops one machine hammering,
per identifier stops a botnet spreading attempts on one account across
many addresses. Neither substitutes for the other.
DummyPasswordHashBase64 / DummyPasswordSaltBase64 are deliberately absent.
Left blank, the application derives a decoy credential at startup from a
value nobody knows, at the CURRENT iteration count. Pinning one here would
freeze it at whatever count was in force the day it was written, and a
decoy that is cheaper than a real hash reopens the timing hole it exists
to close. Set them only if every node must agree on the same decoy.
PortalBaseUrls build the links in reset and invite emails, so they must
be addresses the USER reaches — the Angular apps, not this API.
Auth.//portalBaseUrls: One per app. A reset link into the wrong app lands on a login page that will never accept its token.

//: One origin per app (decision 2.17). These are exact-match, so a dev
server that lands on a different port is refused — which is the loud
failure we want rather than a silent one.
